evidence.note: Explicit correctness-first staging: writes a correct PyTorch/cuBLAS forward pass first ('prioritizes correctness ... later we can optimize if benchmarks indicate issues'), with a small correctness check as the done-criterion before any performance work.

Distinct optimization stage gated on benchmarks: builds a bench harness, times representative shapes, then the full 10 shapes to decide whether optimization is even needed — a clear stage boundary between 'correct' and 'fast'.

Freezes a correct baseline (cp kernel.py kernel_prev.py) and repeatedly restores it after failed experiments, treating a known-good version as a milestone anchor — evidence of disciplined staging beyond mere implicit ordering.

Optimization decomposed into discrete experiments (concat projections, non-contiguous matmul, einsum contraction, fused Triton final), each with a rough exit test — a small correctness smoke test plus a per-shape benchmark — and reverted if wrong or slower.
max-autotune experiment caught by a correctness smoke test (maxdiff ~0.105, allclose False) and reverted, showing per-milestone done-checks prevented a fast-but-wrong regression.

reasoning: The agent clearly separated a correctness-first baseline (naive PyTorch impl with a smoke check) from a later optimization stage gated on benchmarks, and each optimization experiment had a rough success check plus a frozen good baseline to revert to — this exceeds the plain implicit-ordering of anchor 3 and matches anchor 5's 'reference, correct kernel, then optimize with rough checks,' with the frozen-baseline/per-experiment revert discipline pushing slightly above (6). It falls short of 8 because correctness was verified only on a few shapes rather than the full shape/dtype/mask/Cauchy grid, and no independent oracle was constructed (the deliverable itself served as reference), so exit tests were not concrete across the domain.
